chunks: I asked Abā ʿAbdِ اللَّهِ عليه السلام about the saying of Allah,
“like a good tree, whose root is firm and whose branch is in the sky.”

He said: “Rasūl Allah صلى الله عليه وآله is its root, and Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام is its branch. The Imams from their progeny are its branches, the knowledge of the Imams is its fruit, and their Shiʿah, the believers, are its leaves.”
“Is there any increase in it?” He said: I said, “No, by Allah.” He said: “By Allah, when a believer is born, a leaf grows on it, and when a believer dies, a leaf falls from it.”

key_terms.أَصْلُهَا: its root; interpreted here as Rasūl Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams from the holy progeny who are described as the branches
key_terms.شَجَرَةٍ طَيِّبَةٍ: the blessed tree used as a Qur’anic parable for a pure and divinely rooted reality
key_terms.شِيعَتُهُمُ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ: their Shiʿah, the believers, described here as the leaves
key_terms.عِلْمُ الْأَئِمَّةِ: the knowledge of the Imams, described here as the fruit of the tree
key_terms.فَرْعُهَا: its branch; interpreted here as Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام
key_terms.وَرَقُهَا: its leaves, symbolizing the believing followers connected to the tree

ai.seo_question: How do the Imams عليهم السلام interpret the Qur’anic parable of the good tree?
ai.summary: This narration explains the Qur’anic parable of the good tree as referring to Rasūl Allah صلى الله عليه وآله, Amīr al-Muʾminīn عليه السلام, the Imams عليهم السلام, their knowledge, and their Shiʿah. It presents the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام and their wilayah as a divinely rooted, living reality whose growth and signs are seen in the community of believers.
